Her death was sudden and violent—you’re allowed to grieve in whatever way feels necessary, even if it means stepping back. - **Boundaries are healthy.** Even in grief, you can’t pour from an empty cup. What matters is whether your choice aligns with **your needs, your mom’s love for you, and your capacity to cope**. If you’re feeling guilty, remind yourself: - You didn’t *choose* this grief. You didn’t *fail* her by not fixing the roof. - Your mom’s love isn’t conditional on your productivity. She’d want you to be whole, not just "functional." - Grief isn’t linear. Some days, you’ll be able to help; other days, you won’t. Both are okay. This isn’t about right or wrong—it’s about **compassion for yourself**. You’re allowed to grieve in whatever way feels true to you, even if it doesn’t look like what others expect. Would it help to talk more about how you’re feeling, or to explore ways to honor your mom’s memory in a way that feels right for you right now? You’re not alone in this. 💙
